transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
The Hollywood industry has a new powerhouse.
Paramount's parent company, Skydance,
has formally acquired Warner Brothers Discovery.
NPR's Mandalit Del Barco reports on what this means
for major assets in entertainment and news,
and for the people they employ.
David Ellison is growing his media empire
with what will now be known collectively as Skydance,
which he secured for more than $111 billion.
The company merges two legendary movie studios,
Paramount Pictures,
and Warner Brothers Pictures.
Skydance also combines their streaming services,
cable channels, and news outlets CNN and CBS News.
The mega deal faced protests from actors, writers,
and others worried about the concentration of power
and political interference,
but it ultimately passed legal and regulatory challenges
in the U.S. and abroad.
Ellison is starting out with a huge debt,
and those who fought to block the merger worry
there will be job cuts.
Mandalit Del Barco, NPR News, Los Angeles.
- A source tells NPR that the reason
the U.S. military recently withdrew its bombers
from a base in the United Kingdom
was because of a threat of an Iranian drone attack.
NPR's Quill Lawrence reports the U.S. removed
all 12 of its long-range B-1 bombers Sunday.
- A U.S. government official not authorized
to speak publicly confirmed to NPR
that fears of a drone attack on behalf of Iran
caused the U.S. to withdraw all the American bombers
from Fairford Air Base in England.
The base has been used for bombing sorties
in the U.S. and Israeli war with Iran.
Late last month, British authorities arrested
five men traveling in white vans near the air base
in the pre-dawn hours.
The men were later released after no explosives were found.
British officials say the men remain under investigation
and two more arrests have been made in the past week,
including a British-Iranian dual national.
Quill Lawrence, NPR News.
- German authorities have arrested two people,
including the country's former spy chief,
in connection with suspected espionage. Esme Nicholson
reports prosecutors have not yet commented
on whether the men were spying for a foreign actor.
- Germany's federal prosecutor's office
says Auguste Haning will be brought before a federal judge
on charges that include treasonous espionage
and attempted treason.
Haning, now 80, served as the head of Germany's
foreign intelligence agency, known as the BND,
between 1998 and 2005.
Officers have also arrested a current intelligence officer
named only as Manfred D. for allegedly aiding and abetting
attempted treason and treasonous espionage.
The aid is suspected of providing the intelligence
agency's former chief with thousands of classified documents
in exchange for money.
Haning then allegedly used this information
for his private consultancy work.
- It's NPR News.
- President Trump has approved death by firing squad
for former Army Major Nidal Malik Hassan.
The ex-psychiatrist is on the military's death row
at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas for the 2009 shootings
at Fort Hood, Texas.
Hassan killed 13 people and injured more than 30 others.
Trump approved the firing squad execution less than a week
after the governor of Tennessee ordered a halt
to executions in his state because of a botched attempt
to administer a lethal injection
to convicted murder, Krista Pike.
Her attorneys say she was left unconscious
and on life support.
The finalists for this year's National Book Awards
have been announced in fiction.
Author Edwidge Danticop was nominated for the third time
and the nonfiction finalists include examinations
on parenthood, prison, and music.
Here's NPR's Andrew Limbong.
- Edwidge Danticop's novel "Day" is about a woman
surviving an attack on a mall in Miami.
Danticop is up against novelists Morgan Thomas,
Valeria Lucelli, Huyendel Garo-Lopera,
and Henna Lilith Assadi.
Whose book "Paradiso 17" follows a Palestinian man
displaced from his home in 1948.
Over in nonfiction, Colin Asher's book "The Midnight Special"
looks at how prison and music influenced each other.
That book is up against two memoirs
looking at parenthood from different angles,
a memoir about surviving an Egyptian prison,
and a book of political and cultural criticism
from someone who used to work in campaign communications.
The awards are set for Wednesday, November 18th.
Winners get a $10,000 prize.
Andrew Limbong, NPR News.
- I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: Skydance formally acquires Warner Brothers Discovery in $111 billion deal, combining major studios and news outlets
U.S. military withdrew 12 B-1 bombers from UK base due to Iranian drone attack threat
German authorities arrest former spy chief Auguste Haning on espionage and treason charges
President Trump approves death by firing squad for former Army Major Nidal Malik Hasan
National Book Awards finalists announced; Edwidge Danticot nominated for third time in fiction category
